Contact ⓘRepresents a person associated with an account.

Opportunity ⓘRepresents a sale or pending deal.

REFERENCE

Glossary

Search common terms and abbreviations used throughout the guide.

Jump to
A
A

Agentforce

An AI-assisted Salesforce experience that can help draft communication, summarize information, and support case documentation. Its output should be reviewed, edited, and confirmed before use.

A

AI Investigation Tools

Assistive AI tools that can summarize investigation context, suggest possible next steps, surface Knowledge, or reduce manual work. Their output still requires evidence-based human verification.

A

Apex

Salesforce server-side programming language used for custom business logic that runs in Salesforce transactions.

A

Apex Trigger

Apex code that executes in response to record events such as create, update, delete, or undelete.

A

API

Application Programming Interface. A defined way for software or integrations to interact with Salesforce programmatically. In configuration, an API name is the technical name used to reference an object or field, for example Project__c or Start_Date__c.

A

App Launcher

The nine-dot “waffle” used to switch between Salesforce apps and find available items.

A

Approval Process

An automated review workflow in which a record must meet entry criteria and then move through one or more approvers before final approval or rejection actions occur.

A

Assembled

A workforce management tool used for schedule, availability, and coverage processes.

A

Auto-Response Rule

A rule that automatically sends an email response to a Lead or Case submission based on record attributes.

A

Autolaunched Flow

A Flow without screens that is typically invoked by another Flow, Apex, or automation process.

B
B

B2B

Business to Business. A business model where a company sells products or services to another organization. In Salesforce, a common customer model uses an Account for the organization and Contacts for the people associated with it.

B

B2C

Business to Consumer. A business model where a company sells products or services directly to individual consumers. Salesforce implementations can use Person Accounts for this model when the feature is enabled.

B

BANT

Budget, Authority, Need, and Timeline, a qualification framework used to determine whether a lead is a good sales fit.

B

BlackTab

Administrative console used to support customers and troubleshoot org issues.

B

Bulkification

Apex design that processes collections of records efficiently instead of doing repetitive work one record at a time.

C
C

Case

The central support record used to track a customer issue from intake through investigation, communication, and resolution.

C

Case Feed

A timeline-style feed on a case that shows actions, updates, emails, and collaboration tied to the support record.

C

Child Case

A related case linked under a parent case so the issue can be tracked separately while remaining connected to a broader problem.

C

Cross Filter

A report filter that asks a relationship question, such as Accounts with Opportunities or Contacts without Cases.

C

CRUD

Create, Read, Update/Edit, Delete, the object-permission model used to define what actions a user can perform.

C

CSAT

Customer Satisfaction: a measure of how satisfied customers are with the support they received, commonly captured through surveys.

C

Customer 360 (C360)

The Salesforce concept that connects products and customer data across the platform so business functions can work from a broader customer view.

D
D

Dashboard

A visual collection of components powered by source reports.

D

Data Import Wizard

A Salesforce browser based guided tool for straightforward CSV imports.

D

Data Loader

A Salesforce client tool for larger or more complex bulk data operations through Salesforce APIs.

D

Dataloader.io

A cloud based browser data tool that authenticates to Salesforce using OAuth.

D

Debug Level

A setting that controls how much detail Salesforce records in Debug Logs.

D

Debug Logs

Execution records used to reconstruct what happened during a Salesforce transaction.

D

Dependent Picklist

A picklist whose available values are filtered by the value selected in a controlling field. Example: Country controls which State or Province values are available.

D

Developer Console

An in-platform Salesforce environment used for SOQL queries, Debug Logs, and Apex-related runtime inspection.

D

DML

Data Manipulation Language operations that insert, update, delete, or otherwise change Salesforce records.

D

Duplicate Rule

The duplicate-management rule that determines what Salesforce does after a potential duplicate is detected, such as allowing, warning, or blocking.

D

Dynamic Dashboard

A dashboard that displays data using the logged in viewer context.

D

Dynamic Forms & Actions

Lightning capabilities that conditionally show or hide fields and actions based on criteria such as record data or user context.

E
E

Einstein for Service

Salesforce AI-assisted capabilities for service work, such as case summarization, Knowledge suggestions, and drafted responses that still require human validation.

E

Email Logs

Evidence about outbound email sent from a Salesforce org, useful for separating Salesforce sending from downstream mail delivery issues.

E

Entitlement

A support eligibility or service commitment record that can define what level of service a customer should receive.

E

Exception

A runtime error that identifies where execution failed. The exception location is a starting clue and may not be the underlying root cause.

E

Experience Cloud

A Salesforce platform for building branded digital experiences such as customer portals, partner portals, employee communities, microsites, storefronts, listings, and self-service help centers.

E

External ID

A field that stores an identifier from another system and can be used for matching during Upsert.

F
F

Feature License

An additional license that enables a specific feature or capability for an eligible user.

F

Field

An attribute stored on a Salesforce object. Examples include Account Name, Case Status, Opportunity Amount, and custom fields such as Budget__c.

F

Field-Level Security (FLS)

Controls whether a user can see and/or edit individual fields across Salesforce access paths.

F

Filter Logic

The AND and OR expression used to combine multiple report filters.

F

Flow Builder

The visual interface used to read and build Salesforce Flow automation, including the Toolbox, Canvas, Elements, and Resources.

F

Flow Orchestrator

A Salesforce capability that coordinates longer multi-step processes involving multiple flows, approvals, or people.

F

Forecast Category

A sales forecasting classification such as Pipeline, Best Case, Commit, Closed, or Omitted that helps leadership estimate expected revenue.

F

Salesforce Flow

Salesforce declarative automation platform used to build business processes with connected visual elements.

G
G

GHO

Global Handover Template: the internal handover format used to capture the receiving skill group, issue, reproduction steps, and troubleshooting performed before a case moves between teams.

G

Governor Limits

Platform limits that protect shared multi-tenant Salesforce resources during execution.

G

GUS

An internal search for engineering or product work used to determine whether a behavior has already been investigated or reported.

L
L

Lead

An unqualified potential customer or prospect that can move through qualification, nurturing, and conversion.

L

Lead Assignment Rule

A rule that evaluates ordered criteria and assigns a Lead to a specified user or queue. The first matching active-rule entry determines the assignment path.

L

Lead Conversion

The process that turns a qualified Lead into established customer/sales records: an Account and Contact, with an Opportunity created when applicable.

L

Login Hours & IP Ranges

Profile-level controls that can restrict when and from which network ranges a user can log in.

M
M

Manager Groups

Sharing groups based on User manager relationships rather than only the Salesforce Role Hierarchy.

M

Manual Sharing

One-off access granted to a specific record without changing the overall sharing model.

M

Matching Rule

The duplicate-management logic that determines how Salesforce identifies potentially duplicate records by comparing selected fields.

M

Metadata

The structural layer of a Salesforce org, objects, fields, layouts, rules, flows, and other configuration that define how the org behaves.

M

Milestone

A time-based service checkpoint used with Entitlements to track whether support commitments such as response or resolution targets are met.

M

Modify All Data

An elevated administrative permission that grants broad data modification capabilities across the org.

M

Multi-tenancy

An architecture model where multiple customers share underlying infrastructure while each customer org and its data remain isolated.

O
O

Object

A Salesforce data structure used to store records for a business concept. Standard examples include Account, Contact, Case, and Opportunity. A customer-specific example is Project__c.

O

Omni-Channel

Salesforce routing capability that evaluates incoming work and delivers it to an appropriate available agent using configured routing criteria.

O

Opportunity

A Salesforce record used to track a potential sale or deal as it moves through the sales process.

O

Organization History

Broader organization-level and provisioning history, used for questions such as license, limit, or other org-level changes.

O

Organization-Wide Defaults (OWD)

The default record-access baseline for users who do not own the record.

O

OrgFarm

Salesforce internal org-provisioning platform used to spin up preconfigured Salesforce orgs for development and testing use cases.

P
P

Page Layout

A configuration that controls which fields, related lists, buttons, and actions are arranged on a record page for a given assignment.

P

Parent Case

A higher-level coordinating case used to group and monitor related child cases that share a common issue.

P

Permission Set

An additive permission assignment that grants selected access on top of the user Profile.

P

Permission Set Group

A bundle of Permission Sets grouped for assignment around a job function or responsibility.

P

Permission Set License

A license layer that extends the capabilities available to a user beyond the baseline user license.

P

Person Account

A Salesforce record type that combines Account and Contact concepts into one record for business-to-consumer scenarios.

P

Platform Event Flow

A Flow that responds to Salesforce platform events and is commonly associated with event-driven or integration scenarios.

P

POD

Point of Delivery: a logical grouping of Salesforce infrastructure serving customer orgs.

P

Presence Status

An agent availability state used by Omni-Channel to understand whether the agent can receive new work.

P

Product & Topic

Case categorization fields that identify the relevant product area and issue topic. Accurate values help route the case correctly and give the receiving team useful context.

P

Profile

The baseline user access and experience configuration. Each Salesforce user has one Profile.

P

Public Group

An administrator-defined grouping of users, roles, and other members that can be referenced by sharing and other features.

Q
Q

Queue

A holding place for cases or other work before it is assigned or routed to an eligible agent or owner.

Q

Quote

A customer pricing proposal created from an Opportunity and its products. Multiple quotes can exist, but only one can be synced to an Opportunity at a time.

R
R

RCA

Root Cause Analysis: a structured approach for documenting the underlying cause of an issue, the resolution, and the information needed to make the troubleshooting history reusable.

R

reCAPTCHA

An optional Google security service that can help protect Web-to-Lead forms from automated bot and spam submissions.

R

Record Ownership

The ownership relationship that influences responsibility, sharing, and record visibility.

R

Record Type

A configuration that lets one object support different business processes, picklist values, and page-layout experiences.

R

Record-Triggered Flow

A Flow that runs automatically when a Salesforce record is created, updated, or in supported scenarios deleted.

R

Report Type

The reporting data model that defines available objects, relationships, and fields.

R

Restriction Rule

A rule that reduces the records visible to selected users after normal sharing access has been calculated.

R

Role Hierarchy

The Salesforce data-visibility hierarchy that can open record access vertically to users above record owners.

R

Running User

The user context a standard dashboard uses to determine visible data.

S
S

Salesforce Inspector

A browser extension that provides quick access to record data, field and API information, SOQL, and export tools from the current Salesforce context.

S

Salesforce Trust

Salesforce platform-health and maintenance visibility used to distinguish customer-specific issues from broader incidents or maintenance events.

S

Sandbox

An isolated Salesforce environment used for development, testing, training, and safe experimentation without affecting live Production users.

S

Scheduled Flow

A Flow that runs at configured times rather than waiting for a user or record change at that moment.

S

Schema Builder

A visual tool for viewing object relationships and creating custom objects or fields.

S

Screen Flow

An interactive Flow that guides a user through one or more screens to collect or display information.

S

Service Console

A tab-based agent workspace designed for multi-record support work, fast navigation, and productivity.

S

Setup Audit Trail

A history of recent administrative and Setup configuration changes, including who changed something, when, and what action occurred.

S

Sharing Rule

A rule that automatically grants additional record access to defined users, roles, territories, or groups based on ownership or criteria.

S

Skills-Based Routing

A routing model that considers required agent skills in addition to factors such as availability and capacity.

S

SLA

Service Level Agreement: a support commitment that defines response timing or other service expectations.

S

SLO

Service Level Objective: an internal or operational target used to measure whether service is performing as expected.

S

SOQL

Salesforce Object Query Language, used to query Salesforce data.

S

Splunk

A backend event and log investigation tool used when evidence beyond the Salesforce UI or standard Debug Logs is needed.

S

Storm Org

A Salesforce-provisioned demo or test org used by support engineers to reproduce customer issues.

S

Subflow

A reusable Flow called from another Flow so shared automation can remain modular.

S

Swarming

A collaborative support approach where people with relevant expertise work together on the same issue instead of relying only on sequential handoffs.

T
T

Trace Flag

A logging configuration that identifies who or what should be captured in Debug Logs during a defined time window.

T

Triage

The initial assessment of a support issue used to confirm impact, priority, ownership, routing, and the next action.

T

TTR

Time to Resolution: the average time required to completely resolve a case.

U
U

UAT

User Acceptance Testing.

U

Upsert

A data operation that updates a matching record or inserts a new one when no match exists.

U

User License

The primary Salesforce license assigned to a user. It establishes that user's baseline platform capabilities.

V
V

V2MOM

A planning framework that connects methods, measures, and team priorities.

V

Validation Rule

A Salesforce data-quality rule that blocks a save when its configured formula evaluates to TRUE.

V

View All Data

An elevated administrative permission that can provide broad record visibility across the org.

W
W

Web-to-Lead

An out-of-the-box Salesforce feature that generates an HTML form used to submit information from a website and create Lead records in Salesforce.

W

Workbench

A web-based Salesforce API tool for querying data, inspecting metadata or object information, and performing API data operations.

No glossary terms found.

Success Engineer & Case Operations

1 Learn→ 2 Understand→ 3 Investigate→ 4 Apply→ 5 Check
01.1 · LEARNING TOPIC

Support Engineer Role

A Success Engineer combines technical investigation, clear customer communication, and product expertise to help customers move from a reported issue to a useful outcome.

FOUNDATION
01
LEARN

What the role is built around

ROLE FOCUS

Technical Support with customer impact

The role brings together technical investigationReviewing the issue, evidence, environment, and relevant technical context to understand what is happening., customer communication, and product knowledge. Solving the technical problem matters, but so does helping the customer understand what is happening and what comes next.

◎
Customer success

Support work is connected to customer outcomes and service excellence.

⌘
Product expertise

Strong product knowledge makes investigation and guidance more effective.

?Support engineering can develop into deeper technical ownership or broader customer-facing technical paths as product depth, communication strength, and investigation skill grow.
↗
Continuous growth

Product proficiency, certifications, AI readiness, and continued learning are part of the role.

02
UNDERSTAND

See the role from different angles

THE CORE ROLE

Role Focus

A Success Engineer works at the intersection of the customer problem, the product, and the technical evidence needed to move the investigation forward.

01Understand the issue
02Investigate with evidence
03Communicate the next step
03
INVESTIGATE

Use the role as an operating lens

01Technical context

Understand the reported behavior and gather the evidence needed to investigate it.

02Customer context

Understand what the customer is trying to accomplish and communicate progress clearly.

03Product context

Use product knowledge to validate behavior and determine the most useful next action.

04
APPLY

Put the role together

PRACTICE SCENARIO

A customer reports that a core process stopped working.

Your role is not only to find a technical explanation. You also need to understand the customer impact, investigate with evidence, use the right product knowledge, and keep the customer informed about the next step.

Technical investigation+Product expertise+Customer communication

Case Lifecycle

A support case moves through a repeatable journey from creation to closure. Each stage should preserve enough context for the investigation to continue without unnecessary rework.

9 STEPS
01
LEARN

Explore what happens at each stage

CURRENT STEP
1

Case Created

The customer opens a support case and it enters the support workflow.

In practice

The case record becomes the central place for the investigation, communication, and history that follow.

02
UNDERSTAND

What needs to move with the case

01Context

Keep the reported problem, affected behavior, and relevant customer context clear.

02Evidence

Record what was reviewed, reproduced, learned, or ruled out during the investigation.

03Continuity

Document enough detail so a transfer, escalation, or follow-up can continue without restarting from zero.

03
INVESTIGATE

Protect continuity before the next step

01
Current stage

Be clear about where the case is in the lifecycle and what has already happened.

02
Known evidence

Carry forward the useful investigation details instead of making the next step start from zero.

03
Next action

Make the next owner or customer action clear so the case can continue moving.

✦
Core principle

Clear communication, thorough investigation, and useful documentation keep the case moving toward resolution while preserving continuity.

04
APPLY

Choose the next action from the stage you are in

PRACTICE SCENARIO

You have just received a newly assigned case with an unclear error report.

The next move is not to transfer it immediately or change configuration. Start with the initial investigation: review the case and evidence, gather context, and ask the questions needed to understand the behavior.

Review→Clarify→Investigate

01.3 · LEARNING TOPIC

Severity, Business Impact & SLA

Severity defines urgency, business impact explains why the case matters, and SLAService Level Agreement: a support commitment that defines response timing or service expectations. Click to open the glossary. / SLOService Level Objective: an operational target or milestone used to measure support performance. Click to open the glossary. commitments shape the timing of customer communication and follow-up. The right classification comes from the real customer impact, not only from the wording in the case.

PRIORITIZATION
01
LEARN

Recognize what drives urgency

CORE IDEA

Urgency should match the real impact

A case becomes more urgent when the customer experiences stronger business disruption, tighter timing requirements, or broader operational risk. The severity label should reflect that real impact and guide the response model that follows, including the expected SLAService Level Agreement: the support timing commitment attached to the case. Click to open the glossary. behavior and internal SLOService Level Objective: the target used to track whether support is operating on time. Click to open the glossary. milestones.

!
Severity

The urgency level of the case and the speed of response it requires.

▣
Business impact

What is blocked, who is affected, how broad the issue is, and whether core work has stopped.

⏱
SLA & milestones

Timing commitments such as initial response and follow-up that must be monitored and met.

02
UNDERSTAND

Classify the case with the right lens

CLASSIFICATION LENS

What to confirm first

Before accepting a severity at face value, confirm the actual business disruption, customer urgency, scope, and support expectation.

Business disruptionHow much the issue interrupts or blocks the customer’s business process. Scope of impactHow broad the issue is: one user, one team, one feature, or a wider business area. Customer timelineThe customer’s real timing need for a response, update, or resolution path. SLA commitmentsThe response and follow-up commitments attached to the case.
S1Critical

Highest-priority customer situations with major business impact that require immediate coordination and strict milestone attention.

S2High

Serious impact, but not the most critical state. Response urgency is still high and milestones matter closely.

S3Moderate

Important issue with manageable short-term risk. The customer needs progress, but the case is not an emergency.

S4Low

Low-impact questions or issues with limited urgency. Support still follows through, but the timing expectation is lighter.

03
INVESTIGATE

Validate the classification before acting on it

01Confirm the impact

What business process is affected? Is the customer blocked, degraded, or asking a general how-to question?

02Confirm the scope

Is it one user, one record type, one environment, or a broader outage affecting multiple users or functions?

03Confirm the expectation

Use customer communication to align on the real response timeline. If urgency is lower than stated, reclassify it clearly.

✦
Practical note

If the customer confirms they can wait longer, it can be appropriate to lower the severity and manage the case against the more accurate expectation.

PRACTICE SCENARIO

A customer opens a severity 2 case and says users cannot save opportunitiesOpportunity: a Salesforce record used to track a potential sale or deal. Click to open the glossary..

Do not rely only on the initial label. First confirm whether all users are blocked or whether the issue is limited. Ask what response timing the customer needs. If the impact is narrower and the customer agrees a next-day follow-up is acceptable, you can reclassify the case and continue with the more accurate severity.

Scope→Impact→Expectation→Severity

01.4 · LEARNING TOPIC

Case Quality & Documentation

A high-quality case should make the issue understandable, the investigation traceable, and the next action obvious. Good documentation protects continuity so another engineer can continue without rebuilding the investigation from zero.

CASE QUALITY
01
LEARN

Build a case that someone else can continue

CORE PRINCIPLE

Document the investigation, not just the outcome

The case should preserve what happened, what was checked, what evidence was found, and what comes next. A useful record lets the next engineer understand the investigation without reconstructing it from email history.

⌖
Product & Topic

Accurate categorization improves routing and gives the receiving team immediate context.

≡
Case summary

Consolidate the important case information into one usable overview instead of forcing a reader through the entire thread.

Illustration of where the Case Summary action appears in the case actions menu.
✦
AgentforceAI-assisted support experience used to help draft communication and summarize case information. Review, edit, and confirm the output before using it. Click to open the glossary.

Use AI assistance as a draft or summary aid, never as a substitute for technical review.

02
UNDERSTAND

The four questions a strong investigation should answer

DOCUMENTATION LENS

Useful information is actionable information

A form can be complete and still be unhelpful. The goal is to capture enough detail to reproduce the behavior, understand what has already been tested, and continue with the next logical action.

Specific symptoms Evidence Reasoning Next action
01What is happening?

Describe the actual behavior, expected behavior, affected users, environment, and any precise error or identifier.

02How is it reproduced?

Record repeatable steps, the user or context used, and the conditions needed to see the problem.

03What was learned or ruled out?

Capture troubleshooting performed, evidence collected, comparisons made, and paths already eliminated.

04What happens next?

State the next investigation step, customer dependency, handoff need, or resolution action clearly.

03
INVESTIGATE

Check whether the record can support a real investigation

CASE QUALITY CHECK

Before you rely on the case, verify the basics

  • 01
    Issue is specific

    The subject and description identify the real problem rather than repeating the same vague sentence.

  • 02
    Scope is visible

    You know which users, environments, or records are affected.

  • 03
    Reproduction is usable

    The steps are precise enough for another engineer to try the behavior consistently.

  • 04
    Evidence is preserved

    Logs, error IDs, queries, screenshots, or other relevant findings are connected to the reasoning.

AVOID

“It does not work.”

This tells the next engineer almost nothing about the actual behavior, scope, reproduction path, or troubleshooting history.

AIM FOR

Observable + reproducible + traceable

Describe the behavior, record the exact reproduction path, capture what was tested, and show why the next step makes sense.

04
APPLY

Turn a weak case note into a reusable investigation record

WEAK NOTE

“User gets an error when saving. Please investigate.”

No affected-user context, no exact error, no reproduction steps, and no record of what has already been checked.

BETTER RECORD

Make the investigation portable

Capture the affected user, exact action, exact error or ID, environment, reproduction steps, evidence reviewed, troubleshooting already performed, and the next action.

05
CHECK

01.5 · LEARNING TOPIC

Case Closure & Special Processes

Closing a case means leaving a reliable record of the outcome and following the correct process for the situation. Unresponsive customers, duplicate cases, out-of-scope requests, and root-cause documentation require different closure decisions.

CLOSURE
01
LEARN

Close the case for the right reason

CLOSURE PRINCIPLE ?These closure principles are developed further in Case Follow up and Closure Process. Click to open the related reference.

The case should end with a clear outcome, not just a Closed status.

A useful closure leaves enough context to understand what happened, how the case ended, and which process justified the final action.

01Resolved

Document what solved the issue and why the resolution is complete.

02Unresponsive

Use the defined no-response process and preserve the follow-up history.

03Duplicate

Preserve the original case and close the duplicate with a clear comment.

04Out of scope

Validate the boundary and record the guidance provided to the customer.

02
UNDERSTAND

Match the closure path to the situation

NO RESPONSE

Unresponsive customer process

No-response handling depends on the stage of the case. The general unresponsive-customer path uses a 10-day response window, while a case already in Solution Provided can automatically close after 5 business days without a customer reply.

Follow up→Document→Close by process
03
INVESTIGATE

Build a closure record that is reusable

WHERE DO THESE FIELDS COME FROM?

They appear as part of the Close Case process.

When the investigation is complete and you choose Close Case, the closure process asks the engineer to classify why the issue occurred and document the result. These are fields on the support case, they are not separate cases.

Important

Sub-Cause is not “Sub Case.” It is a more specific classification underneath Case Cause. Its available values depend on the Case Cause selected first.

01Case Cause

The primary category that best describes why the issue occurred.

02Sub-Cause

A more detailed classification under Case Cause. It behaves as a dependent picklist, so the options shown depend on the selected Case Cause.

03Root Cause Analysis

The written summary of what the investigation discovered: the underlying cause, the resolution, and the reasoning that supports the conclusion.

04Product Feature

A closure field that identifies the product capability related to the case. Confirm that the Product Feature associated with the case is correct before finalizing closure.

04
APPLY

Choose the correct closure path

PRACTICE SCENARIO

You provided the solution, documented the resolution, and the customer has not replied.

Keep the case history clear and follow the correct post-solution no-response process. If the workflow reaches the automatic-closure condition after 5 business days without a response, the case can close without treating it as an unresolved investigation.

Solution documented→Follow-up→No reply→Process closure

01.6 · LEARNING TOPIC

Transfers & Escalations

A transfer should continue the investigation, not restart it. Before moving a case, validate scope, choose the correct destination, and carry enough context for the receiving team to understand the issue and the work already performed.

HANDOFF
01
LEARN

Move the case without losing the investigation

CORE PRINCIPLE

Research first, transfer second

Do not move a case to another team or a higher level with no context. Confirm scope, perform the initial research, and make the handoff useful enough that the next team can continue immediately.

⌖
Product & TopicCase categorization fields used to describe the product area and issue topic. Accurate values help route the case correctly and give the receiving team immediate context. Click to open the glossary.

Use these case categorization fields to identify the relevant product area and issue topic. Accurate values support routing and give the receiving team immediate product context.

✓
Scope validation

Use the relevant Knowledge guidance after initial research to determine whether the request belongs to the current team.

⇄
Handover quality

Explain the issue, reproduction steps, troubleshooting performed, and why the case is moving.

02
UNDERSTAND

Use a transfer decision path

01
Research the request

Understand the issue before deciding whether it belongs somewhere else.

→
02
Validate scope

Use the relevant support Knowledge article or guidebook to confirm team responsibility.

→
03
Select the destination

Choose the appropriate skill group, internal team, or partner path.

→
04
Complete the handover

Transfer the investigation history, not only the case record.

03
INVESTIGATE

Build the handover the receiving team needs

GHOGlobal Handover Template: the internal handover format used to preserve the receiving skill group, issue, reproduction steps, and troubleshooting history. Click to open the glossary. HANDOVER DETAILS

What should travel with the case

The receiving team should be able to understand where the case is now, why it is moving, and what work has already happened.

01Current skill group

Document where the case currently lives.

02Skill group to hand over to

Identify the receiving destination clearly.

03Issue

Briefly describe the problem and include the relevant error message.

04Steps to reproduce

List the steps if they are not already populated. If unknown, make the pending reproduction action explicit.

05Troubleshooting performed

Record the investigation already completed, including relevant debug, network, or Splunk analysis.

06Why the transfer is happening

Inform the receiving team why ownership is moving and what the expected next action is.

04
APPLY

Decide whether to transfer, escalate, or redirect

INTERNAL TRANSFER

The issue is outside your team scope, but another internal team owns the product area.

Validate the scope, document Product & Topic, preserve the issue and troubleshooting history, and explain why the receiving team is the correct owner.

PARTNER / OUT-OF-SCOPE

The issue belongs to a partner application rather than Salesforce support.

Do not pretend the investigation belongs to the Salesforce team. Redirect appropriately and, when useful, provide the customer information about where partner support can be found.

ESCALATION RULE

Never escalate an empty case.

Research first. An escalation without context forces the next level to repeat basic discovery and breaks the continuity the handoff is supposed to protect.

05
CHECK

Confirm the handoff standard

01.7 · LEARNING TOPIC

Queue & Work Management

Support work is not handled in the order it happens to appear. Queues organize incoming work, Omni-ChannelOmni-Channel evaluates incoming work and routes it to an appropriate available agent. Click to open the glossary. distributes it, and engineers continuously balance availability, capacity, skills, priority, and SLAService Level Agreement: the support timing commitment attached to a case. Click to open the glossary. risk.

WORK MANAGEMENT
01
LEARN

Understand how work gets organized before an engineer touches it

CORE IDEA

Right work → right person → right time

Routing exists to reduce manual assignment, balance workload, and help customer work reach an engineer who is actually able to take it.

AvailabilityCapacitySkillsPriority
Q
QueueA holding place for cases or other work before assignment or routing. Click to open the glossary.

Organizes work before it is assigned to the right eligible agent or owner.

O
Omni-ChannelSalesforce routing capability that evaluates incoming work and delivers it to an appropriate available agent. Click to open the glossary.

Evaluates routing criteria and distributes work automatically.

P
Presence StatusAn availability state that tells Omni-Channel whether the agent can receive new work. Click to open the glossary.

Communicates whether an agent is available, busy, away, at lunch, or offline.

02
UNDERSTAND

See what Omni-Channel evaluates before routing work

01Availability

Is the agent currently able to receive new work?

02Capacity

How much active work can the agent realistically handle?

03Skills

Does the agent match the expertise required for the work item?

04Priority

How urgently should this work be handled relative to other work?

ROUTING ENGINE
◎

Omni-Channel

Combines the configured routing criteria and delivers the work to the best eligible available agent.

PRESENCE STATUS

Availability must stay accurate

AvailableCan receive work BusyDo not route new work AwayTemporarily unavailable Lunch / BreakDo not route new work OfflineNot active
SMARTER ROUTING

Skills-Based RoutingA routing model that considers required skills in addition to availability and capacity. Click to open the glossary.

After Omni-Channel and skills-based routing are enabled, administrators can configure skills and route work only to agents who meet the required combination.

SpanishPortugueseBillingService CloudSales CloudCPQ
03
INVESTIGATE

Prioritize the queue by risk, not by convenience

QUEUE PRIORITIZATION

Work smarter, not simply top-to-bottom

Prioritize the cases with the greater SLA risk first. Severity, approaching milestones, aging, customer follow ups, and new lower risk work help shape that decision.

  1. 1
    Critical / high-severity work

    Handle the most urgent customer impact first.

  2. 2
    SLA at risk

    Protect cases approaching a response or follow-up commitment.

  3. 3
    Aging cases

    Prevent work from sitting without meaningful progress.

  4. 4
    Customer follow-ups

    Keep commitments and previously promised next steps moving.

  5. 5
    New / lower-risk work

    Pick up new work while higher-risk obligations remain protected.

01Wrong queue?

Review the routing configuration and determine why the work was directed to the current queue.

02Not routed?

Check agent availability, capacity, routing requirements, and skill eligibility.

03Unexpected assignment?

Confirm the configured business priority and whether another eligible agent was actually available.

04
APPLY

Follow the routing decision in a realistic workload

PRACTICE SCENARIO

A new customer case enters the queue while three engineers have different availability states.

Sarah is Available. Mike is Busy and already handling high-priority work. Jessica is at Lunch. Omni-Channel should not assign randomly: it evaluates who is eligible and available, then routes the new work to Sarah.

S
SarahAvailable
Receives work ✓
M
MikeBusy / high-priority load
Protected
J
JessicaLunch / Break
Unavailable

01.8 · LEARNING TOPIC

Customer Experience

Strong support is more than finding the technical answer. The customer should understand what is happening, what has been learned, who owns the next action, and when they can expect the next update.

ART OF SERVICE
01
LEARN

Build the customer experience around five communication habits

ART OF SERVICE

Technical confidence + human clarity

A useful customer experience combines technical progress with professional, empathetic communication. Customers should never need to guess whether the case is moving or what happens next.

Listen→Investigate→Explain→Follow through
01Customer communication

Be clear, professional, empathetic, and customer-centered.

02Effective case updates

Keep updates concise and actionable while documenting findings and next steps.

03Setting expectations

Communicate timelines, ownership, dependencies, and changes before the customer has to ask.

04Difficult conversations

Use empathy, professionalism, de-escalation, and solution-oriented language.

05Executive communication

Focus on business impact, risk, status, and mitigation rather than unnecessary technical detail.

02
UNDERSTAND

Turn investigation progress into a useful case update

SE
Customer updateClear enough to reduce the next follow-up question

Hi Customer, I reviewed the behavior and confirmed that the issue is reproducible under the affected configuration. I am validating the remaining differences before recommending a change. I will update you again by tomorrow with either the confirmed cause or the next investigation step.

01
What did I do?

State the investigation action or research completed.

02
What did I find?

Share the useful result, evidence, or current understanding.

03
What happens next?

Set the next action, owner, and expected timing.

Expectation rule

An update can still be valuable before the root cause is known. Tell the customer what is being explored and when they should hear from you again.

03
INVESTIGATE

Recognize when communication needs more care

CUSTOMER SIGNALS

Do not wait for frustration to become an escalation

Customers commonly escalate when they feel the case is not progressing. Strong communication reduces that uncertainty and helps internal teams coordinate earlier when risk increases.

01
Listen for the real concern

Separate frustration about the experience from the technical symptom itself.

02
Acknowledge without arguing

Do not tell the customer their issue is unimportant. Clarify the impact and respond professionally.

03
Use evidence

If a request is out of scope or a limitation applies, support the explanation with the appropriate documentation.

04
Coordinate early

If dissatisfaction or business risk is increasing, align with the appropriate internal stakeholders instead of letting the situation drift.

EXECUTIVE UPDATE
Business impactWhat is affected?
→
Current riskWhat can worsen?
→
MitigationWhat are we doing now?
→
Next checkpointWhen will we update again?
04
APPLY

Protect continuity when you are out of office

OUT OF OFFICE IN ORGCS

Set expectations before you step away

Use the Out of Office message in OrgCS so teammates and customers know when you are unavailable, how long you will be away, and what they should do for urgent needs.

01
Enable Out of Office

Turn on the Out of Office message so your availability status is clearly communicated.

02
Select dates

Choose the start and end dates that define the exact period when you will be unavailable.

03
Add your message

Write a short message that explains you are out, mentions limited email access if relevant, and tells urgent contacts where to go.

04
Save the setup

Save the configuration so the message becomes active in OrgCS during the selected time window.

OUT OF OFFICE IN GOOGLE CALENDAR

Block your time so availability is visible to everyone

After setting the OrgCS message, reserve the same time in Google Calendar so teammates can quickly see your availability and plan around it.

01
Add event

Click Create (+) in Google Calendar and open a new event.

02
Add details

Give the event a clear title such as OOO or Out of Office.

03
Set date & time

Enter the start date, end date, and time range that match your unavailability.

04
Add message

Include a short note about your availability and return date when it is useful for internal visibility.

05
Save

Save the event so your OOO block appears on your calendar and others can see the coverage window.

Coverage reminder

In addition to setting the OrgCS OOO message, notify customers that need coverage, reflect the time in Google Calendar, and update AssembledAssembled is the workforce management tool used for schedule and availability tracking. Click to open the glossary. so workforce visibility stays aligned.

Expectations, Metrics & Career

Support performance is measured through a combination of workload, customer experience, resolution speed, service commitments, escalation behavior, workforce adherence, knowledge contribution, and continued role development.

SUCCESS SIGNALS
01
LEARN

Read the five core support metrics as different signals

SUPPORT METRICS

No single metric tells the whole story

Each measure answers a different operational question: how much work is moving, how customers feel, how long resolution takes, whether commitments are being met, and how often work requires another support layer.

P
Productivity

Amount of work completed through cases solved, tasks completed, workload handled, and throughput.

Efficiency & capacity
C
CSATCustomer Satisfaction: the customer’s rating of the support experience. Click to open the glossary.

Customer satisfaction with the support received, commonly measured through survey scores.

Experience & quality
T
TTRTime to Resolution: the average time required to completely resolve a case. Click to open the glossary.

Average time required to completely resolve a case.

Speed & efficiency
S
SLAService Level Agreement: a commitment to respond or resolve within a defined timeframe. Click to open the glossary.

Measures whether target response and resolution commitments are being met.

Customer commitment
E
Escalation Rate

Percentage of cases requiring another team, engineering, or a higher support tier.

Complexity & troubleshooting
02
UNDERSTAND

Connect the metric to the behavior it is trying to protect

METRICWHAT IT MEASURESWHY IT MATTERS
ProductivityCases, tasks, workload and throughputShows efficiency and available capacity.
CSATCustomer survey resultsReflects service quality and the customer experience.
TTRResolution time across resolved casesShows the speed and efficiency of the support motion.
SLACases meeting response / resolution commitmentsProtects contractual and customer expectations.
Escalation RateEscalated cases relative to total casesSignals case complexity and troubleshooting effectiveness.
✦
Use the metric in context

These measures work as complementary signals. Operational quality includes both the work completed and the experience created while completing it.

Salesforce & Customer 360

Salesforce is a platform of connected applications and services. Customer 360Customer 360 connects Salesforce products and customer context across business functions. Click to open the glossary. is the mental model that helps you see those products as one ecosystem instead of isolated tools.

PLATFORM VIEW

LEARN

CURRENT PRODUCT
⚡

Sales

02
UNDERSTAND

One platform, different business functions

CUSTOMER 360

The products are different, but the customer journey is connected

Sales, Service, Experience, Commerce and other products can participate in the same customer lifecycle. The final implementation varies by company, industry, and business process.

01Infrastructure

Salesforce provides the underlying platform services.

02Applications

Core and specialized products support different business functions.

03Customer context

Related data creates continuity across the journey.

04Customization

Organizations extend the platform with their own apps and processes.

03
INVESTIGATE

Do not troubleshoot a connected issue as an isolated product

01Identify the business function

Which cloud or product experience is the customer working in when the behavior occurs?

02Trace the shared context

Which accounts, contacts, cases, opportunities, or other records connect the workflow?

03Find the boundary

Determine whether the issue belongs to one product configuration or to the interaction between products and shared data.

✦
Support mindset

Customer 360 is useful because customer problems often cross product boundaries. Start by understanding the complete journey before narrowing to a component.

04
APPLY

Map a cross-product customer question

PRACTICE SCENARIO

A service agent says the customer context they expect from a sales process is missing.

Do not begin by assuming Service Cloud is broken. Identify which record or relationship should carry the context, confirm where the data originates, and determine whether the issue is in the source data, the connection between records, or the consuming experience.

Business function→Shared record→Connection→Product behavior

02.2 · LEARNING TOPIC

Salesforce Architecture

Architecture gives a Success Engineer the context to decide whether a behavior is customer-specific, org-specific, environment-specific, or part of a broader platform condition.

INFRASTRUCTURE
01
LEARN

Understand multi-tenancy and PODs

SHARED INFRASTRUCTURE

Multi-tenancyMultiple customers share the underlying Salesforce infrastructure while each customer's org data stays isolated. Click to open the glossary.

A single Salesforce software and infrastructure model serves multiple customers while each tenant remains logically isolated.

ORG A

Customer data isolated

ORG B

Customer data isolated

ORG C

Customer data isolated

POD
Point of Delivery

A logical infrastructure cluster serving a set of customer orgs. POD context helps support teams understand infrastructure scope and release context.

02
UNDERSTAND

Use the architecture tools that support investigation

BTBlackTabAdministrative console used to support customers and investigate org details. Click to open the glossary.

Administrative support console for customer org investigation. BT environments are used for Production context, while SBT environments are used for Sandbox context.

OFOrgFarmInternal org-provisioning platform for preconfigured Salesforce environments. Click to open the glossary.

Provision preconfigured orgs for development and specialized testing use cases.

?Slack Channel: #orgfarm
STStorm OrgsSalesforce-provisioned demo/test orgs used to reproduce issues. Click to open the glossary.

Demo and test orgs used by support engineers to reproduce customer behavior.

TRSalesforce Trust

Public platform health view for incidents, maintenance, and service transparency.

03
INVESTIGATE

Decide whether the problem is isolated or broader

01Customer org

Confirm the exact org and environment where the behavior occurs.

→
02POD context

Understand the infrastructure cluster serving the org.

→
03Platform health

Check Salesforce Trust for a broader incident or maintenance condition.

→
04Comparison

Use another environment or test org to determine whether the behavior reproduces elsewhere.

04
APPLY

Use scope before escalation

PRACTICE SCENARIO

A customer reports an unexpected platform error.

Capture the org and environment first. Check whether the behavior is isolated, review platform-health context, identify the POD when relevant, and compare against another org or environment before deciding that the issue is a broader platform defect.

Org→Environment→POD / Trust→Compare

02.3 · LEARNING TOPIC

Environments

Production runs the real business. SandboxesIsolated Salesforce environments used for development, testing, training, and safe experimentation. Click to open the glossary. give teams a safer place to build, reproduce, and validate behavior.

SAFE TESTING
01
LEARN

Production and Sandbox have different risk profiles

LIVE

Production

Real customers, real revenue, live automations, dashboards, and daily business operations.

  • Observe carefully
  • Protect customer data
  • Avoid configuration changes during investigation
VS
SAFE TEST

Sandbox

An isolated copy or test environment used for development, testing, training, and experimentation.

  • Reproduce safely
  • Validate changes
  • Experiment without affecting live users
02
UNDERSTAND

Choose the sandbox type that matches the purpose

DDeveloper

Metadata-only and lightweight. Useful for individual development and testing.

DPDeveloper Pro

Similar to Developer with more storage capacity.

PCPartial Copy

Metadata plus a subset of production data for more realistic testing.

FFull

Complete metadata plus production data for the highest fidelity sandbox copy.

03
INVESTIGATE

Check environment differences before calling it a defect

01Identify the environment

Production, Developer, Developer Pro, Partial Copy, or Full?

02Check the refresh

If Production changes are missing in the sandbox, verify the last refresh timestamp.

03Compare data & configuration

Different data volume or stale configuration can explain inconsistent behavior.

04Verify entitlements

Sandbox type, quantity, and refresh availability can depend on edition and licensing.

!
Production safety rule

Do not make configuration changes in a customer's live Production org while investigating. Observe or reproduce the issue, then move testing to an appropriate sandbox or test org.

04
APPLY

Explain a Production / Sandbox mismatch

PRACTICE SCENARIO

A field exists in Production but the customer cannot find it in their sandbox.

Before treating it as a platform defect, confirm the sandbox type and the last refresh. Then compare metadata and data differences between Production and the sandbox.

Sandbox type→Refresh date→Metadata→Data
05
CHECK

Confirm safe-environment reasoning

QUICK CHECK

1. What is Production?

2. Which sandbox contains metadata and a subset of production data?

02.4 · LEARNING TOPIC

Editions, Licenses & Entitlements

What a customer can use may depend on the Salesforce edition, the user's primary license, additional license layers, and organization-level entitlements.

FEATURE ACCESS
01
LEARN

Separate edition, user access, and add-on capability

ORG
Salesforce Edition

Sets the broad product capability, limits, and sandbox entitlement available to the organization.

↓
01User LicensePrimary baseline license assigned to a Salesforce user. Click to open the glossary.

Baseline capabilities required for the user.

02Feature LicenseAdditional license that enables a specific feature for an eligible user. Click to open the glossary.

Adds a specific feature or tool.

03Permission Set LicenseLicense layer that extends capabilities beyond the base user license. Click to open the glossary.

Extends the user's available capabilities.

02
UNDERSTAND

Entitlements explain what the organization is allowed to consume

LICENSE ≠ CONFIGURATION

A missing feature is not automatically a bug

Before investigating deeply, verify whether the customer's edition and license combination actually includes the expected capability.

Edition limits

Feature availability and platform limits can vary by edition.

Sandbox entitlements

Available sandbox types, quantities, and refresh intervals can depend on edition/licensing.

Usage-based entitlements

Some organization capabilities are consumed or purchased based on usage rather than a user seat.

User-specific layers

One user's capability may differ from another because of license assignments.

03
INVESTIGATE

Use a license-first troubleshooting sequence

01Confirm feature expectation

What feature is the customer trying to use?

→
02Verify edition

Does the organization edition include the feature?

→
03Verify user licenses

Does the affected user have the required license layers?

→
04Then inspect configuration

Only after access is valid should you assume a configuration issue.

04
APPLY

Explain why one user is missing a feature

PRACTICE SCENARIO

A feature works for one teammate but is unavailable to another.

Compare the users' primary licenses, feature licenses, and permission set licenses before treating the difference as a platform defect. Then review configuration and permissions if licensing is correct.

Edition→User License→Add-ons→Configuration

02.5 · LEARNING TOPIC

Data Model

Successful troubleshooting starts by separating metadataThe structural blueprint of the org: objects, fields, layouts, rules, and other configuration. Click to open the glossary. from the data stored inside those structures.

STRUCTURE & RECORDS
01
LEARN

Start with the blueprint / content distinction

BLUEPRINT

Metadata

ObjectsAn object is a Salesforce data structure that stores records for a business concept. Examples include Account, Contact, Case, Opportunity, and a custom object such as Project__c. Click to open the glossary., fieldsA field stores one attribute on an object. Examples include Account Name, Case Status, Opportunity Amount, or Start_Date__c on a custom Project__c object. Click to open the glossary., page layouts, validation rules, flows, classes, and other configuration define what the org can do.

STRUCTURE → CONTENT
RECORDS

Data

The actual records and values stored inside the configured structures for the customer's business.

02
UNDERSTAND

Objects and fields create the shape of the data model

OBJECT

ObjectA Salesforce data structure that stores records for a business concept. Examples include Account, Contact, Case, Opportunity, and Project__c. Click to open the glossary.

Think of an object as the category of information being stored. Examples include Account for companies, Contact for people, Case for support issues, and Project__c for a customer-specific project structure.

FIELD

FieldA field stores one attribute on an object. Examples include Account Name, Case Status, Opportunity Amount, or Budget__c on a custom object. Click to open the glossary.

Think of a field as one attribute stored on that object. Examples include Account Name, Case Status, Opportunity Amount, or a custom field such as Budget__c.

OBJECT EXAMPLES

These are Salesforce objects, connected through relationships

Each card represents an object that can contain many records. The labels below distinguish standard objects provided by Salesforce from a customer-defined custom object.

STANDARD OBJECTAccountCompanies or organizations
STANDARD OBJECTContactPerson associated with an account
STANDARD OBJECTOpportunitySale or pending deal
STANDARD OBJECTCaseSupport issue
CUSTOM OBJECTCustom_Object__cCustomer-defined structure
Standard vs Custom

Salesforce provides standard objectsObjects store records for a business concept. Standard examples include Account, Contact, Case, Lead, and Opportunity. Click to open the glossary. such as Account, Contact, Case, Lead, Opportunity, Product, Quote, Task, and User. Customers can create custom objects and fieldsFields store attributes on an object. Examples include Status, Amount, Start Date, or a custom field such as Budget__c. Click to open the glossary. for business-specific needs. Their APIApplication Programming Interface, or API, is a defined way for software or integrations to interact with Salesforce programmatically. In this context, an API name is the technical name used to reference an object or field. Click to open the glossary. names commonly use the __c suffix.

CUSTOM OBJECT EXAMPLE

Project__c

A custom object can combine standard fields such as Name and OwnerId with custom fields created for the customer's business process.

Field LabelField API NameData Type
Project NameNameText
DescriptionDescription__cLong Text Area
Start DateStart_Date__cDate
StatusStatus__cPicklist
BudgetBudget__cCurrency
OwnerOwnerIdLookup(User)
AccountAccount__cLookup(Account)
HOW A CUSTOM FIELD BECOMES USEFUL

From configuration to business use

Creating the field is only the first step. It also needs to appear in the right user experience and then participate in the processes that depend on it.

◇01Create the field

Choose the label, API name, data type, and field-level options.

→
▤02Add it to the experience

Place the field on the appropriate page layout or Lightning record experience.

→
◫03Use it on records

Users can view or edit the field when visibility, permissions, and page configuration allow it.

→
▥04Use it in processes

The field can support reports, filters, formulas, validation, Flow, and other automation.

COMMON CUSTOM FIELD TYPES

Choose the field type based on the data and behavior you need

Hover or select a type to see what it stores and a practical example.

CURRENT FIELD TYPE
T

Text

Stores short text such as a project code, external reference, or customer identifier.

EXAMPLEProject_Code__c → “MX-2026-001”
03
INVESTIGATE

Ask whether the problem is structural or record-specific

METADATA

“The field does not exist / the layout is wrong / the rule blocks save.”

Inspect configuration: object, field, layout, record type, validation rule, automation, or visibility logic.

DATA

“The field exists, but this record has the wrong or missing value.”

Inspect the specific record values, related records, imports, updates, and the process that populated the data.

04
APPLY

Choose the right investigation branch

PRACTICE SCENARIO

A user says a customer value is missing from a record.

First confirm whether the field itself exists and is part of the expected configuration. If the structure is correct, move to the record data and related process that should populate the value.

Field exists?→Configuration correct?→Record value→Source process

02.7 · LEARNING TOPIC

Configuration

Configuration determines how Salesforce presents business processes to users. Setup, Object Manager, relationships, record types, layouts, picklists, and dynamic visibility are common starting points for investigation.

ADMIN FOUNDATION
01
LEARN

Know where configuration lives

⚙
Setup

The administrative control center for platform-wide configuration. Object Manager and Schema Builder are both reached from the Setup experience.

OM
Object Manager

Inspect and configure a specific standard or custom object, including fields, relationships, record types, layouts, and related settings.

?Navigation: Setup → Object Manager. Select an object to open its configuration.
SB
Schema BuilderVisual tool for viewing object relationships and creating custom objects or fields. Click to open the glossary.

Visualize objects, fields, and relationships when the data model is easier to understand as a diagram.

?Navigation: Setup → Object Manager → Schema Builder. You can also locate Schema Builder from Setup navigation.
02
UNDERSTAND

See how record experience is assembled

01
Dependent PicklistsA dependent picklist shows values based on the selection made in a controlling field. Click to open the glossary.

The controlling field filters the values available in the dependent field.

02
Record TypesAllow one object to support different processes, layouts, and picklist values. Click to open the glossary.

Different teams can use the same object while receiving different business-process experiences.

03
Page LayoutsControl fields, sections, related lists, buttons, and actions arranged on a record page. Click to open the glossary.

Assignments combine user context and record type to determine the layout a user sees.

04
Dynamic Forms & ActionsConditionally show or hide fields and actions based on criteria such as record data or user context. Click to open the glossary.

Visibility criteria reduce page clutter and surface only relevant fields and actions.

HOW RECORD TYPES WORK

One object can support different business experiences

Record Types let the same object represent different processes by connecting users to the appropriate business process, picklist values, and page experience.

▣01Create Record Types

Define the distinct business processes the object needs to support, such as New Business and Renewal.

→
▦02Connect the experience

Associate each Record Type with the appropriate page layout and available picklist values.

→
◉03Grant user access

Make the relevant Record Types available to the users or teams that need those business processes.

→
✓04Use the right Record Type

When creating or editing a record, the user works with the Record Type and experience available to them.

HOW TO SET UP A DEPENDENT PICKLIST

Build the dependency from controlling value to valid choices

The controlling field provides the context. Salesforce then limits the dependent field to the values mapped to that controlling selection.

1Create the controlling field

Create the field that drives the selection, for example Country.

→
2Create the dependent field

Create the field whose choices will be filtered, for example State / Province.

→
3Set the dependency

In Field Dependencies, select which field controls the other field.

→
4Map valid values

Choose which dependent values are valid for each controlling value.

→
5Add it to the experience

Place the fields on the appropriate page layout or record experience and test the behavior.

DEPENDENT PICKLIST IN PRACTICE

The record only offers values that are valid for the controlling selection

03
INVESTIGATE

Use a configuration-first path for missing fields or values

01Correct object?

Start in Object Manager for the object where the issue occurs.

→
02Field exists?

Confirm the field and its type.

→
03Record Type / Layout

Verify the user's record type and assigned page layout.

→
04Dynamic visibility

Check whether criteria hide the field or action.

Missing picklist values?

Check the controlling/dependent field relationship and value mapping before treating the missing option as a defect.

04
APPLY

Troubleshoot the user's actual record experience

PRACTICE SCENARIO

A user says a field is visible for another team but not for them.

Confirm the object, then compare the user's record type and page-layout assignment. If those are correct, check Dynamic Forms / Actions and remember that permissions can be another visibility layer covered later in the course.

Object→Record Type→Page Layout→Dynamic visibility

03.1 · LEARNING TOPIC

Sales Cloud Overview

Sales Cloud organizes the path from prospect interest to revenue. A Success Engineer needs the business lifecycle because the fastest investigation starts by identifying the first stage where expected records, ownership, or automation stopped matching the intended process.

CUSTOMER ACQUISITION
01
LEARN

See the complete sales journey before troubleshooting one feature

SALES CLOUD

Interest becomes a managed customer relationship

The process begins with a prospect, moves through qualification and conversion, and then continues through active deal management, onboarding, support, retention, and growth.

01Capture

Prospect information enters Salesforce.

→
02Qualify

Determine whether the prospect is worth pursuing.

→
03Convert

Create established customer/sales records.

→
04Manage Deal

Move the Opportunity through the sales process.

→
05Grow

Onboarding, support, renewals, and additional business.

02
UNDERSTAND

Know which record owns each part of the journey

LLeadAn unqualified potential customer or prospect. Click to open the glossary.

Prospect before conversion.

AAccount

Customer organization or business relationship hub.

CContact

Individual person associated with an Account.

OOpportunityA Salesforce record used to track an active potential sale or deal. Click to open the glossary.

Active sales deal and pipeline record.

QQuoteA customer pricing proposal created from an Opportunity. Click to open the glossary.

Pricing proposal for products/services.

03
INVESTIGATE

Locate the first break in the business process

INVESTIGATION LENS

Where did actual behavior first diverge?

Do not begin with a random setup page. Start with the customer's business outcome and walk backward through the expected records and automation.

01What stage was reached?

Lead capture, qualification, conversion, or Opportunity management?

02What should exist now?

Which Account, Contact, Opportunity, owner, or status was expected?

03What should have run?

Assignment, auto-response, validation, duplicate logic, Flow, Apex, or approval?

04
APPLY

Translate a vague sales issue into a process question

PRACTICE SCENARIO

“Salesforce lost my customer after they filled out our website.”

Break the statement into checkpoints. Was a Lead created? Was it assigned correctly? Was it converted? Which records should have been created? Did the Opportunity progress as expected? The first failed checkpoint defines the next investigation.

Capture→Ownership→Conversion→Deal

03.2 · LEARNING TOPIC

Accounts, Contacts & Person Accounts

These records define who the customer is. Before troubleshooting relationships or record creation, confirm whether the implementation follows a B2BBusiness to Business. A company sells products or services to another organization. Click to open the glossary. model or a B2CBusiness to Consumer. A company sells products or services directly to individual consumers. Click to open the glossary. model, then confirm what Salesforce record structure the customer expects.

CUSTOMER DATA MODEL
01
LEARN

Separate the business relationship from the individual person

B2B MODELBusiness to Business. The customer relationship is usually an organization represented by an Account, with people represented by Contacts. Click to open the glossary.

Account + Contact

AccountOrganization
→
ContactPerson

An Account acts as the relationship hub; Contacts represent the people associated with that organization.

B2C MODELBusiness to Consumer. The customer is an individual consumer, which can be represented with a Person Account when that feature is used. Click to open the glossary.

Person AccountA specialized Salesforce record that combines Account and Contact concepts for an individual customer. Click to open the glossary.

ACCOUNT + CONTACT

For individual-consumer scenarios, Salesforce can represent the customer in a single Person Account record rather than a separate business Account + Contact structure.

ACCOUNT EXAMPLE

Accounts list

Organizations and customer companies are visible as Account records.

CONTACT EXAMPLE

Contacts list

Individual people associated with organizations appear as Contact records.

PERSON ACCOUNT EXAMPLE

Person Accounts list

When Person Accounts are enabled, an individual customer can be represented in a single Account based record.

02
UNDERSTAND

Use Account as the relationship hub

ACCOUNTCustomer relationship hub
Contacts

People and communication context.

Opportunities

Active and historical sales deals.

Cases

Support interactions and customer issues.

Other records

Customer-specific business relationships.

03
INVESTIGATE

Confirm the expected customer model first

01B2B or B2C?

Is the customer modeled as an organization with people, or as an individual consumer?

02Which relationship is missing?

Is the Contact missing its Account, or is another related record not connected as expected?

03Was the record created or converted?

Trace how the record entered the org and whether the expected related records should have been created.

04
APPLY

Avoid using the wrong data model as the baseline

PRACTICE SCENARIO

A user expects a Contact for an individual customer, but only one customer record exists.

Confirm whether Person Accounts are part of the customer's B2C model before concluding that a Contact failed to create. The expected record structure depends on how the org models customers.

Business model→Expected record→Relationship

Find Web-to-Lead in Setup

UNDERSTAND

What is in scope for support?

SUPPORTED BASELINE

Standard, Setup-generated, unaltered form

Use the standard generated HTML as the comparison point. Record Type is the permitted modification in the standard support scope guidance.

OUTSIDE THAT BASELINE

Heavy custom modification

Custom JavaScript, altered form structure, third party frameworks, and custom CSS can move the issue outside the standard support troubleshooting scope.

IN SCOPESalesforce-side configuration

Generated form behavior, field mapping, validation impact, duplicate rules, Lead creation, Assignment Rules, and Auto-Response Rules are part of the Salesforce path.

OUT OF SCOPECustom website implementation

Custom scripts, external site builders, third-party wrappers, and modified HTML/CSS structures should be isolated from the Salesforce baseline before escalating the issue as a platform defect.

R
reCAPTCHAGoogle's optional anti-bot service used with Web-to-Lead. Click to open the glossary.

Useful for reducing automated spam. Because it is a Google-managed service, isolate whether reCAPTCHA is blocking legitimate submissions rather than treating every failure as a Salesforce defect.

03
INVESTIGATE

Find the exact failure point

FORMNo Lead created

Confirm the customer is using the standard form and determine whether submission reaches Salesforce.

SPAMBot submissions

Review reCAPTCHA usage and identify the source before assuming a Salesforce-side block.

OWNERWrong assignment

Move to Lead Assignment Rules once the Lead is created successfully.

EMAILNo acknowledgement

Inspect the active Auto-Response RuleA rule that sends automatic email responses based on record attributes. Click to open the glossary., criteria, template, and email delivery evidence.

LIMITSubmission limit reached

Check org and limit context in the support tooling rather than guessing from the website symptom.

04
APPLY

Use the standard form as a control test

PRACTICE SCENARIO

A highly customized website form no longer creates Leads.

Reproduce with the standard setup-generated form. If the standard form works, the evidence points away from the Salesforce baseline and toward the customization layer. If the standard form also fails, continue with Salesforce configuration, validation, duplicate logic, reCAPTCHA isolation, and limits.

Standard form→Submission→Lead created?→Next automation

→

Work is Routed

Work is delivered instantly to the right agent when the configured routing requirements are met.

→

  • Updates the customer

Happy customer, efficient team.

Escalation Rules

Case Escalation Rules are time-based automations that monitor qualifying cases and take action after a configured amount of time. Their behavior depends on criteria, the active rule, the escalation clock, and the business hours that apply.

Assignment Rules determine initial ownership using case criteria such as origin, product, priority, language, or region.

ESCALATION RULE
What should happen after time passes?

Escalation Rules monitor cases that meet defined criteria and take configured action after enough qualifying time has elapsed.

▽

→
↗
3
Takes Action

Reassigns, updates fields, or notifies the right people after qualifying time passes.

→
♢
4
Keeps Moving

Helps cases receive attention and continue toward resolution instead of sitting unnoticed.

Timing still matters:criteria + clock start + business hours + elapsed qualifying time

05.1 · LEARNING TOPIC

Security Model, Who Sees What?

Salesforce security is layered. The fastest access investigation starts at the lowest relevant layer and only moves upward after that layer is confirmed.

ACCESS LAYERS
01
LEARN

Build the security stack from the bottom up

Record access expands as additional sharing mechanisms are applied↗
01
OWDBase level of record access

Organization-Wide Defaults establish the baseline visibility for records a user does not own.

02
Role HierarchyOpen up access vertically

Managers can gain access through the hierarchy when the object respects hierarchy-based sharing.

03
Sharing RulesOpen up access laterally

Ownership-based or criteria-based rules extend record access to defined users, roles, territories, or groups.

04
Flexible SharingOpen up access for specific needs

Manual Sharing, Apex Sharing, Teams, and Queues can provide additional access for particular records or work patterns.

Baseline Object and Field Permissions

Record-sharing mechanisms only matter after the user already has the required object permission and Field-Level Security.

02
UNDERSTAND

Connect the security concept to effective access

01Login / authentication

Can the user enter the org?

02Object access

Can the user access the object at all?

03Field access

Can the user see or edit the required field?

04Record baseline

What does OWD allow for records the user does not own?

05Additional sharing

Do hierarchy, rules, teams, groups, or manual shares open access?

06Restrictions / elevation

Is a Restriction Rule filtering access, or is an admin permission bypassing normal behavior?

03
INVESTIGATE

Use the right checks in the right order

01

Confirm the user can log in before troubleshooting record visibility.

02

Confirm object permission before investigating sharing.

03

Confirm FLS before assuming a page or record-sharing issue.

04

Identify OWD, then evaluate mechanisms that open or restrict record access.

04
APPLY

Apply the model to an access symptom

PRACTICE SCENARIO

Work from evidence, not assumption

A standard user cannot see an Account that an administrator can see. Do not start with Sharing Rules. First compare login context, object permission, field access if relevant, OWD, ownership, hierarchy/sharing, restriction rules, and elevated admin permissions.

Login→Object→Field→Record baseline→Sharing→Restrictions

05.3 · LEARNING TOPIC

Permission Sets

Permission Sets add access on top of the Profile so exceptions and job-specific capabilities do not require a separate Profile for every combination of responsibilities.

ADDITIONAL ACCESS
01
LEARN

Use Permission Sets to extend, not replace, baseline access

Use Permission Sets to extend, not replace, baseline access

Permission Sets can add object, field, system, app, or feature permissions. Permission Set Groups bundle multiple Permission Sets around a job function.

01Profile

Baseline access for the user.

02Permission Set

Adds selected access for an exception or responsibility.

03Permission Set Group

Bundles multiple Permission Sets into a reusable assignment.

04Effective access

Profile plus all assigned Permission Sets and groups.

See the group as a wrapper around multiple permission bundles

A Permission Set Group gives admins one clean assignment while still letting each inner Permission Set focus on a specific capability area.

Permission Set 2

Permission Set 3

Keep permissions modular while the group delivers them together.

Sharing Rules

Sharing Rules automatically open additional record access to defined users, roles, territories, or groups when the baseline and hierarchy do not provide enough visibility.

AUTOMATIC RECORD SHARING
01
LEARN

Use Sharing Rules to open access consistently

CORE IDEA
